comparison: Both strongly support the crosslinking data (C28-C34, C38) demonstrating Fis-Hin DBD proximity. Peer reviewers praised experiments as 'clever and comprehensive.' OpenEval emphasizes convergence of structural, biochemical, and functional data. Peer review also addresses C4 and notes concern about mutant folding (C35-C37) was resolved by controls, while OpenEval separates these rescue experiments into a different result.

Perfect agreement on site-specific crosslinking data (C39-C40) showing asymmetric Fis-Hin contacts. Both evaluations find the evidence strongly supported. Peer reviewers included this as part of 'clever and comprehensive' experiments without raising concerns.

Both address helix-B mutagenesis and knotting data (C41-C46), but with different assessments. OpenEval finds the evidence strongly supported with convergence of functional and topological data. Peer reviewers find the explanation 'reasonable' but express uncertainty (UNCERTAIN), noting 'one can't help but think that perhaps something else is going on' and questioning the mechanism for multiple rotations and knotted products.

OpenEval addresses FeBABE scission and enhancer mutagenesis data (C47-C51) as supported evidence for helix-B-DNA contacts. Peer review groups these claims with helix-B functional data (C41-C46) and expresses uncertainty about the overall mechanism, questioning whether alternative explanations involving product DNA interactions might apply.

Both support the disulfide-locked Hin dimer experiments (C52-C54, C68) demonstrating Fis interaction with inactive dimers. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental design and controls. Peer reviewers praised these as part of 'clever and comprehensive' experiments without raising concerns.

Both address ligation data (C55-C56, C75) showing Fis-Hin association doesn't inhibit the final chemical step. OpenEval finds this strongly supported. Peer review groups this with the disulfide experiments and supports the conclusion that enhancer remains associated with Hin throughout the reaction.

Both address the structural model (C58-C61). OpenEval finds it well-constrained by experimental data and supported by conservation analysis (C62-C65). Peer reviewers support the model but note presentation issues, stating it's 'sometimes hard to follow' structural features and requesting better labeling.

OpenEval includes conservation analysis (C62-C65) as strong support for the structural model. Peer reviewers find this 'one of the most interesting findings' but express uncertainty (UNCERTAIN), challenging the conservation claim by stating 'the number of K and R near the end of helix B doesn't look significantly different in the invertases vs resolvases' and requesting better discussion.

Perfect agreement on topological analysis (C70-C74). Both find the evidence supported. OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic soundness and consistency with experimental observations. Peer reviewers found the control experiment 'very satisfying' and the topological explanation plausible, though requested clarification of the explanation.

Both address comparative analysis across serine recombinases (C76-C81). OpenEval finds this well-supported and strengthening the proposed mechanism. Peer reviewers express uncertainty (UNCERTAIN), finding it interesting but challenging the conservation claims and questioning whether contacts merely stabilize complexes or actively promote remodeling.

Both address background/established knowledge claims (C1, C6-C27). OpenEval notes these are well-established with appropriate citations providing essential context. Peer reviewers treat these as accepted foundational knowledge without questioning them.

OpenEval synthesizes multiple lines of evidence including Fis-dimer interactions (C67-C69) and regulatory functions (C2, C4, C18, C20-C23) as supported. Peer review addresses some overlapping background claims but doesn't specifically evaluate the synthesis of Fis-dimer interactions and supercoiling requirements as a distinct result.

OpenEval includes rescue experiments (C35-C37) as part of supporting crosslinking data specificity for Fis-activation. Peer reviewers evaluate these rescue experiments separately, praising them as 'nice experiments' showing helix B mutations are only needed if Fis is present, but suggest better contextualization with Sin experiments.

OpenEval includes model overview (C57) as part of structural model evaluation. Peer review includes C57 in background claims, treating it as established context rather than a new finding requiring evaluation.
